A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OFMU work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison; retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on TOFU, WMDP, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, together with robustness, sensitivity, and component analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses, revises reported results, and adds empirical runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same inner forgetting objective, gradient-similarity penalty, stationarity reformulation, and two-loop updates. Newly specified penalty scheduling and default inner-step counts document implementation choices without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TOFU, WMDP Biosecurity/Cybersecurity with MMLU utility, and CIFAR-10/100. Forgetting scenarios and paraphrase, multi-hop, and cross-lingual probes are retained. The new resource measurements use existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Original forgetting/utility comparisons retain their comparator sets. New runtime comparisons in v2 Table 12 extend participation, including GA/GradDiff on WMDP and GradDiff/NPO/SimNPO/RMU on CIFAR, beyond those benchmarks' v1 comparisons. Correcting RMU's expanded name does not establish a replacement implementation; BLUR–NPO appeared only in v1's WMDP prose, not its results table.

E3.justification: v1 Table 3 reports Biosecurity and Cybersecurity accuracy as utility; v2 Table 5 instead specifies unlearning efficacy as 1 − accuracy, substantially changing the meaning of these evaluations. MMLU remains accuracy. Appendix 7.5.13 also introduces runtime normalized to a GA update and memory normalized to a forward-only pass. The metric revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix 7.5.13 adds an efficiency analysis, including runtime sensitivity to T = 5 versus T = 10 and memory-cost comparisons. Existing component ablations, hard-sample robustness, forget-set sensitivity, embedding alignment, and penalty/inner-step performance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Tables 1–3 and 5 newly report means and standard deviations over five runs for TOFU, CIFAR-10, and WMDP, replacing unqualified point estimates. WMDP also gains a p < 0.05 significance assertion without an identified test. Existing three-seed robustness results and five-forget-set dispersion remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an increase from a previously specified main-experiment run count.

E6.justification: TOFU and CIFAR-10 values are revised; for example, OFMU's LLaMA-3.2 forget01 FQ changes from 0.93 to 0.91 ± 0.04. New Tables 12–13 quantify previously unreported costs: TOFU runtime is 2.85× GA at T = 5 and 4.22× at T = 10, while LLaMA memory is 3.1× a forward-only pass. WMDP results are replaced under changed metric semantics and cannot be read as direct performance improvements. CIFAR-100 and existing ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix 7.3.2 expands explicit non-convex assumptions, adds an outer-iteration term to the final gradient bound, and removes v1 Equation 36's objective-gap bound. New Appendix 7.4 derives inner-loop, outer-loop, and total computational costs, including Θ(KTBd). These are substantive mathematical additions and revisions, although they do not establish that the convergence argument is now valid.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: hierarchical forgetting, similarity-aware gradient decorrelation, scalable two-loop optimization, convex/non-convex convergence guarantees, and strong forgetting–utility trade-offs. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The WMDP discussion reinterprets hazardous-domain scores from preserved answering ability to removal of hazardous knowledge, materially changing what those results support. New efficiency discussion attributes practical scalability to small inner budgets and HVP computation. However, retained utility-preservation language and Appendix 7.5.10's accuracy description conflict with the revised WMDP interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix 7.5.12 newly specifies ρ0 = 0.3, multiplicative growth γ in [1.5, 2.0], the four-value initialization grid, reuse across models and forget ratios, and default T = 5. Resource-analysis details also identify normalization references and memory components. Existing hardware, optimizer, batch size, learning rate, and model-access links are retained.

R1.justification: WMDP and the baseline-list description of RMU are reattributed from Bu et al. to Li et al., correcting links to distinct prior works already present in the bibliography. The bibliography and broader research positioning remain unchanged; Fan and Maini citation updates refer to works already cited.

P1.justification: v2 adds computational-complexity and resource-analysis subsections, locally rewrites WMDP discussion, and makes small wording and publication-header edits. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained. Some reference handling deteriorates, including an unresolved citation in Appendix 7.3.2 and 'Tables ??–5' in Appendix 7.5.7.

P2.justification: The combined TOFU table is split into separate architecture tables, uncertainty reporting changes table presentation, and three new complexity/runtime/memory tables are added. Appendix floats are repositioned, including Figure 4. All five figure graphics are retained unchanged; the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: Five-run uncertainty reporting, explicit penalty-tuning details, and measured resource costs make v2 more informative and reproducible than v1. The improvement is limited by unresolved substantive problems: WMDP's revised metric conflicts with its retained metric description, the significance test is unspecified, and the revised convergence bound retains non-vanishing terms despite claiming epsilon-stationarity. The reporting gains support a limited net improvement, rather than a substantial repair of the paper's evidential and theoretical weaknesses.
